protocol: Independent review under D-000; refute not confirm; subject is the contract adopted D-032 requires before host doctor acts
summary: The contract conforms to adopted D-032 on almost every axis I could test at bytes, and two of those tests came out better than the artifact needed to. Its four CA-3 subtypes — OUT_OF_ROOT_READ, LOCAL_SOCKET_OR_PIPE, KEYCHAIN, PRIVILEGED_PLATFORM_FACILITY — are an exact match for the four effects BLK-2 enumerates, with none dropped and none invented, and KEYCHAIN is correctly routed to DR-108 and held unexercisable. The outcome vocabulary is exactly D-032's mandatory minimum, is marked closed, and expressly excludes COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION and DR-105's grant-outcome INDETERMINATE as non-members. It mints nothing: both PT- occurrences are references and one is the disclaimer 'Does not mint PT-* tokens', the single occurrence of SATISFIED is the negative 'Does not discharge DR-105 or DR-114 SATISFIED', and the sweep for waiver language returns zero. One blocker stands. D-032 names exactly one question as belonging to this contract — the execution side of slice-1 doctor egress — and the artifact returns it marked UNSETTLED with no owner and no route, which is the circular-deferral shape BLK-5 identified, recurring in the successor that was supposed to end it.

findings.claim: Adopted D-032 assigns exactly one open question to this contract by name — the execution side of slice-1 doctor egress — and the artifact returns it unanswered, naming no owner and no route by which it is ever settled.
findings.evidence: Adopted D-032 in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md reads, in its decision paragraph: 'Slice-1 doctor egress execution side remains for that contract.' 'That contract' is this artifact's own self-description: authorityClaim states 'This artifact PROPOSES the scoped host-effect authorization contract D-032 requires…'. The artifact's response, at coveredActs.CA-4-host.slice1ExecutionSide, is: 'UNSETTLED which slice-1 doctor egress is host vs component; until settled, host CA-4 is fail-closed unless explicitly consented and this contract instance exists.' No owner is named, no successor artifact is named, and no route is given. Nothing unsafe follows — the fail-closed posture is preserved and stated — so this is not a waiver. It is an undelivered assignment, and its shape is the one this corpus has already adjudicated: BLK-5 in the join verdict at 538f368156d22f96bf067dd9faad924610dd78ca16968ad46541efcf14a61344 reads 'Circular deferral on the one question the join turns on: DR-105 /tensionsObserved/2 defers "is a doctor consent a journal grant?" to DR-114's owner; doctor [defers back]'. D-032 discharged that instance by answering it. This artifact reproduces the pattern one level down: D-032 defers the egress side to the contract, and the contract defers to nobody. A candidate whose function is to be the terminus of routed questions cannot leave the single question routed to it in the same state it arrived.
findings.proposedFix: Either settle it — state whether slice-1 doctor egress is host-executed or component-executed, citing doctor v4 or D-002 — or re-route it lawfully: name the owning authority and the artifact in which it is decided, and record that this contract does not settle it, so the assignment is transferred rather than dropped. If the honest answer is that the fact cannot be settled before the doctor fixture surfaces exist, say that and name the fixture gate.

findings.claim: The artifact never names a join blocker, so a reader cannot tell from its bytes which of the four blockers D-032 routed here it addresses and which it leaves open.
findings.evidence: Measured: the substring 'BLK-' occurs zero times in the artifact. Adopted D-032 routes four blockers to this contract — 'Join blockers: BLK-1/2/3/4 STILL-ROUTED as above' — where BLK-1 is CA-2's execute-anything gap, BLK-2 the four tokenless CA-3 effects, BLK-3 the outcome vocabulary, and BLK-4 the grant journal against doctor's read-only fixture. The artifact does address three of them substantively: coveredActs.CA-2 carries the DR-119 requirement for BLK-1, coveredActs.CA-3's four subtypes answer BLK-2, and outcomeVocabulary.mandatoryMinimumPerD032 answers BLK-3. BLK-4 is handled by consent.lifecycle's 'Not journaled as a DR-105 grant' plus outcomeVocabulary.notGrantJournalOutcomes. So the substance is present and nothing is waived — the sweep for 'DISCHARG' and 'WAIV' returns zero on both. What is missing is the accounting. Every prior candidate in this corpus records its routed obligations by id, and D-032's own bytes state the four by number; without that mapping this artifact cannot be checked against its own charter, and the next reviewer must reconstruct it as I did.
findings.proposedFix: Add a joinBlockerDisposition block naming BLK-1, BLK-2, BLK-3 and BLK-4, each with the clause of this contract that answers it and its resulting state — noting that BLK-3 stays STILL-ROUTED per D-032 rather than discharged by the vocabulary's mere existence.

findings.claim: The necessary-not-sufficient property is the structural core of D-032's requirement, and only one of its two instances has an acceptance-evidence fixture class.
findings.evidence: Adopted D-032 states the contract 'is necessary, not sufficient, before CA-1 host head, CA-2, CA-3, or host CA-4 is exercisable', and the artifact carries the corresponding gates: coveredActs.CA-2.admissionAlsoRequires names the DR-119 approved exception and ifThirdPartyAlsoRequires names DR-117 and DR-128; coveredActs.CA-1-host-head.admissionAlsoRequires names DR-G21 containment and an admitted manifest. The four fixture classes are FC-FAIL-CLOSED, FC-OUTCOME, FC-TAIL and FC-KEYCHAIN. FC-KEYCHAIN does test one instance of the property — 'KEYCHAIN remains unexercisable while DR-108 is deferred' is precisely a case where this contract is satisfied and the act still is not admitted. No class tests the CA-2 instance, which is the one BLK-1 turns on: that a recorded contract instance plus named consent still does not admit customer-tool execution absent DR-119. Nor does any class test CA-1's DR-G21 gate. The gap is narrower than it first looks, and I record that FC-KEYCHAIN covers the property in kind, which is why this is an advisory rather than a blocker.
findings.proposedFix: Add FC-NOT-SUFFICIENT: with a recorded contract instance and named consent present, CA-2 remains unexercisable while the DR-119 approved exception is absent; and the CA-1 analogue against DR-G21.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: cd3cfd4008bb1b04f3e0c744577ff18ee1433261c9a8967e3cc8b8bb980b6a1f both times. No drift.

Mints no DR-105 token: swept the bytes for 'PT-' and found two occurrences, both references — actorSet.outOfScope naming 'component-originated egress (DR-105 / PT-NET-EGRESS)' and whatThisDoesNotDo's 'Does not mint PT-* tokens.' No new token, effect class, or truth-table entry appears anywhere. authorityClaim states in terms that it 'mints no DR-105 token, no D9 number, and no identity recipe.'

Waives no join blocker: 'WAIV' occurs zero times and 'DISCHARG' occurs zero times in the artifact. Every act it covers is gated rather than released, and the fail-closed rule is stated as an absolute — 'An in-scope host act with no named consent and no recorded contract instance is UNEXERCISABLE… Absence never permits.'

Outcome vocabulary is complete against its charter and correctly bounded. D-032's mandatory minimum is 'completed, definitely-not-performed, unknown/indeterminate'; the artifact carries COMPLETED, DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED and INDETERMINATE, three members, marked closed: true. It also states the exclusion that keeps BLK-3 honest: 'COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION and DR-105 INDETERMINATE-as-grant-outcome are not members. Those remain DR-105 component-tail outcomes.' DEFINITELY_NOT_PERFORMED carries the anti-overclaim gloss 'Not a revoke-undone claim', and INDETERMINATE is scoped to attempts — the failClosed rule confines it to 'when the attempt was made and the result is unknown', so an unattempted act reports CONSENT-REQUIRED rather than borrowing an outcome it did not earn.

KEYCHAIN is fail-closed, and the CA-3 subtype set is exactly right. BLK-2's full text enumerates four effects: 'keychain is RESERVED (DR-108 deferred), local socket / named pipe is RESERVED, out-of-root path read is not in the vocabulary at all, privileged platform facility is unnamed.' The artifact's four subtypes are KEYCHAIN, LOCAL_SOCKET_OR_PIPE, OUT_OF_ROOT_READ and PRIVILEGED_PLATFORM_FACILITY — a one-to-one match with none dropped and none invented. KEYCHAIN routes to 'DR-108; unexercisable while DR-108 is deferred', matching adopted D-032's 'keychain → DR-108, still deferred, unexercisable', and FC-KEYCHAIN carries the corresponding fixture class. I checked the deferral independently: D-002's explicit deferrals include DR-108 for slice 1.

No silent SATISFIED: 'SATISFIED' occurs once, inside whatThisDoesNotDo as 'Does not discharge DR-105 or DR-114 SATISFIED.' The header carries status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL and binds NOTHING. This is consistent with file 08 at 877e36d3, whose DR-105 cell closes 'This row is not SATISFIED' and records the host-effect contract as still required.

Recited counts are honest. Three outcome members against D-032's three; four covered act families against D-032's 'CA-1 host head, CA-2, CA-3, or host CA-4'; four CA-3 subtypes against BLK-2's four effects. No count in the artifact overstates what it enumerates.

D-032 conformity, clause by clause against the adopted bytes: actorSet.inScope is the host under direct instruction with doctor as that surface, and outOfScope is component children and component-originated egress, matching 'component tails stay in DR-105'; consent.carriers are invocation-time naming and pre-existing policy, matching 'invocation or pre-existing policy'; consent.lifecycle is invocation-bound, not journaled as a grant, ended by cancel or process death, matching 'doctor-side invocation-bound record, not a grant'; consent.notCarriers includes self-grant, preserving file 03's law that authority is not self-granted; CA-1-host-head confines the contract to the spawn decision with 'The child's subsequent effects are DR-105'; CA-2 carries DR-119 and the third-party DR-117/DR-128 path.

governingDecisions correctly names both live decisions and their effect: D-032 as adopted with the necessary-not-sufficient and fail-closed-until-recorded conditions, and D-035 with the disclaimer that this artifact 'does not reopen' doctor-contract.v4.

verdictNote: REJECT at one blocker, with three advisories. The rejection is narrow and I want its scope clear: I contest nothing this contract decides. Its actor split, fail-closed posture, consent model, outcome vocabulary and CA-3 routing all conform to adopted D-032, and two of them — the CA-3 subtype set against BLK-2's four effects, and the outcome vocabulary's exclusion of grant-journal outcomes — are more precise than the charter strictly required. The blocker is an omission, not an error: D-032 named one question as this contract's to answer and the artifact hands it back unanswered and unrouted. Settling it, or transferring it to a named owner, is a repair of one field. A v2 doing that and adding the three advisory items would in my view be acceptable.
